svg.text: One iteration of the Day 15 loop on Ray: who calls what, and where the bytes go
Sync mode, CartPole, 2 rollout actors + 1 GPU learner on one node. Solid blue: a remote method call (it returns an ObjectRef at once). Dashed teal: object data. Numbers: order within an iteration.
Owns every object returned by a call it submits.
actors = [RW.remote(i, cfg) for i in range(2)] # ActorHandle
refs = [a.sample.remote(128) for a in actors] # ObjectRefs
for a in actors]) # sync: before the next sample
wait mode: ready, rest = ray.wait(pending, num_returns=1)
in-process memory store (small objects owned by the driver)
Ray's own processes on the node (ray.init starts them, ray stop ends them)
GCS: cluster metadata, the actor directory
· places each actor by its num_cpus / num_gpus; too big = pending forever
· sets OMP_NUM_THREADS = floor(num_cpus) in each worker process
Method calls and small objects go straight between processes (gRPC);
the raylet places actors and manages the shared-memory store.
num_cpus=1, num_gpus=0: OMP 1, and it still sees the GPU
copy w into the torch params; SHA-256 digest
sample(T=128): 4 envs x 128 steps, CPU forward
Calls from one caller run one at a time, in order.
update(*fragments): # Ray resolved both refs before the call
GAE on CPU -> one H2D copy -> PPO on the GPU
ray.put once for all actors; the actors fetch it themselves.
the node reads them without a copy
weights of version v: dict of numpy arrays, 36,620 B
ray.put always writes here, whatever the size
returns of 100 KiB or more land here, not inline
e.g. Exp 3 fragments with 1 or 2 actors
learner.update.remote(F0_ref, F1_ref): refs in; Ray copies the 2 × 21.5 KB values into the call
ray.put(weights): once per version, from the learner
Async mode: ① for iteration k+1 is submitted before ② for iteration k. Calls to one actor run in submission order, so that sample runs after set_weights(vk) and is trained at version k+1: lag 1.
